profile.a: The author, writing an op-ed for the Financial Times for International Finance, with a companion dashboard.
FT readers: bankers, fund managers and UK businesses that buy from emerging economies.
Are emerging market currencies more a risk or an opportunity? The answer given: an opportunity, for those who analyse the risk well.
June 2025, comparing fund holdings in 2017 with today and using the IMF's April 2025 outlook.
Emerging markets, with Colombia as the AI example and Vietnam, Brazil and Mexico as trading partners for UK firms.

Fund managers are pulling back from the dollar amid erratic US policy, and several emerging currencies are outperforming developed ones, yet emerging equities' share of global funds has fallen from 8% to 5%.
Auction theory (Milgrom and Wilson) and Sen's development as freedom as lenses, a Colombian central-bank forecasting example, IMF and Bank of England data, and a local-currency hedging example.

charts.title: Emerging market equities as a share of global equity funds (%)
charts.takeaway: Investors cut their emerging-market weight by more than a third. The op-ed reads this as hesitation rather than weaker fundamentals; it does not rule out the second explanation.

charts.title: Growth forecasts: emerging vs developed economies (%)
charts.takeaway: Emerging economies grow at least twice as fast, the op-ed's case for 'real productivity'. Faster growth is not the same as a stable currency, which the piece treats as one point.
charts.source: Page 165. The developed figure is the upper bound implied by 'half that rate or less'.

charts.takeaway: The verdict depends on telling strong currencies from weak ones; the op-ed does not say how to do that.

charts.title: The practical example: a natural hedge for a UK firm

items.title: Exposure
items.text: A UK business buys materials from Vietnam or Brazil and pays in local currency.

items.title: Action
items.text: It borrows in the same local currency.

items.title: Effect
items.text: Debt and costs move together, so currency swings partly cancel out.

items.title: Result
items.text: More predictable costs and less exposure, turning currency risk into a manageable position.
